\paragraph{The decode defect is on the rollout path --- so we measured whether it reaches the published numbers, rather than asserting that it does not.} ``No number is conditioned on a rollout'' is true of the \emph{rollout} decoder, but it is not by itself a defence, because P2 decodes through a \emph{second}, independent reimplementation (\texttt{experiments/\allowbreak{}cotfaith\_\allowbreak{}edit.py:infer\_\allowbreak{}action}) which had never been compared to upstream at all. It delegates generation to HuggingFace \texttt{generate} rather than running its own masked-argmax loop, so it is closer to upstream than the rollout path is, but it still puts no logit mask over the $256$-token action window --- a non-action token is silently dropped rather than forbidden --- and it does not perform upstream's input-id surgery. Two questions follow and they separate cleanly, so we answer them separately: the de-quantization convention needs no inference at all, and token selection needs a GPU.

\emph{The de-quantization convention: measured, and it does not move $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ at all.} P2 maps bin $b$ to $-1 + (b{+}0.5)\cdot 2/256$, whereas the checkpoint's own tokenizer uses the midpoints of \texttt{linspace}$(-1,1,256)$, a spacing of $2/255$. The two differ by up to $0.007797$, which is $15.6\%$ of $\tau{=}0.05$, and they differ non-multiplicatively at the top of the range: \texttt{linspace}$(-1,1,256)$ has only $255$ midpoints, so bins $254$ and $255$ collapse onto one value, and the gripper sits at bin $255$ in $5{,}634$ of our records. This needs no new inference to settle. P2's map is injective on bin indices, so the bins are exactly recoverable from the floats we release, and both conventions can be replayed over the entire artifact. We did that for all $36{,}688$ scored edit records across all $34$ released edit runs ($0$ failed to invert; $0$ replay disagreed with its own stored $\Delta$). \textbf{$\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ is exactly invariant}: not one record changes its faithful flag and no family's $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ moves by any amount, even though $17{,}058$ records do receive a different $\Delta_\infty$ (max shift $0.007751$). That is structural rather than fortunate, and therefore holds for future runs and not just for these records: a $\Delta$ is always an integer number of bins, and $\tau{=}0.05$ falls strictly between the six-bin and seven-bin quantum under \emph{both} spacings ($0.0469/0.0549$ against $0.0471/0.0549$). Every headline number in this paper --- the whole of Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard}, $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$, and the paraphrase floor --- is an $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ and is unaffected.

\emph{$\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ is a different matter, and we report the corrected values rather than the invariance we would have preferred.} Its predicates test a cosine against $-0.5$, a sign, and an L$_2$ ordering, none of which survives a shift of the value grid. $25$ records change admissibility and $46$ change verdict. The largest single effect is ECoT-bridge's \emph{gripper\_flip}, whose $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ falls from $0.037$ to \textbf{exactly $0$} because $16$ of its $300$ records sit at bin $127$, which P2 places at $-0.003906$ (negative, hence admissible) and the checkpoint places at exactly $0.0$ (inadmissible); on \emph{direction\_flip}, \emph{Ours} data-50B moves from $0.59$ to $0.54$, r=8 from $0.69$ to $0.67$, r=32 from $0.62$ to $0.61$, and the $\cos$ column shifts in the third decimal (at most $0.020$ on any single family mean). Tables~\ref{tab:leaderboard} and~\ref{tab:directional} are stated \emph{under the checkpoint's convention}, which is what \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}derive\_\allowbreak{}metrics.py} now applies to the stored actions before scoring; records that are not on P2's bin grid --- a future checkpoint with a different action tokenizer --- pass through untouched and are counted in the artifact rather than silently forced onto it. The F6 conclusion is unchanged by the correction: ECoT-bridge still ranks first by magnitude and second-to-last by direction. \texttt{experiments/\allowbreak{}p2\_\allowbreak{}dequant\_\allowbreak{}recompute.py} is the derivation and prints both conventions side by side; artifact: \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}p2\_\allowbreak{}decode\_\allowbreak{}equivalence/\allowbreak{}}.

\emph{Token selection: measured, and it is identical --- the audit's own slice was not.} Whether P2's token \emph{selection} matches upstream's --- the thing the rollout decoder failed --- is a GPU measurement rather than a replay, and it has now been run. \texttt{experiments/\allowbreak{}p2\_\allowbreak{}decode\_\allowbreak{}equivalence.py} hands upstream's \texttt{predict\_action} P2's \emph{own} \texttt{input\_ids}, so the chain-of-thought prompt is held fixed and only the decode mechanics differ, then inverts upstream's un-normalized output back to bins through a $(256,7)$ table built from the checkpoint's own tokenizer and own action statistics and recomputes the faithful flag from those bins. On \texttt{ecot-openvla-7b-bridge}, $12$ samples, $66$ prompts and $54$ scored (sample, family) records over five families: \textbf{the raw generated ids are byte-identical on $66$ of $66$ prompts}. Both paths run their own greedy \texttt{generate} on the same \texttt{input\_ids}, so that settles selection directly --- P2's unmasked argmax landed inside the $256$-token action window every time, and its missing logit mask never changed a selected token here. No faithful flag differs on any of the $54$ records and every family's $\mathcal{F}$ is equal to the last digit ($1.00$, $0.90$, $1.00$, $0.50$, $0.92$). The vocab-size confound we had flagged as the larger risk --- upstream indexing the grid from \texttt{text\_\allowbreak{}config.vocab\_\allowbreak{}size} ${-}$ \texttt{pad\_to\_multiple\_of} while P2 uses the processor's tokenizer --- is measured absent: both are $32{,}000$, so the offset is $0$. This confines the $24/24$ rollout mismatch to the rollout path, which publishes no number, at the stated $N$ on this one checkpoint.

\emph{The same audit, on the second architecture family.} That bound was single-checkpoint by construction, so we ran the analogous audit on all three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints, where the decode is not a variant of OpenVLA's but a different mechanism --- a $(10,7)$ chunk read in one forward pass under a hybrid causal/bidirectional mask, out of a $2{,}048$-slot window inside PaliGemma's base vocabulary (compute-platform \texttt{8cvg2daria}, $12$ frames each). On \texttt{deepthinkvla\_\allowbreak{}libero\_\allowbreak{}cot\_\allowbreak{}sft} and \texttt{\_rl} the verdict is \textbf{equivalent on $12/12$ comparable frames}: our \texttt{build\_input\_cot\_ids} reproduces the checkpoint's own \texttt{input\_cot\_ids} byte-identically, \texttt{action\_start\_idx} agrees, and \texttt{decode\_action\_chunk} reproduces the $(10,7)$ chunk exactly (max absolute difference $0.0$, bin centers identical, $0$ errors). \textbf{On \texttt{deepthinkvla\_base} the audit returns \emph{undefined}, not equivalent}: on $12/12$ frames generation never emitted upstream's own stop tail within the $320$ new tokens the edit runs used, so no assembled sequence was ever compared against one the checkpoint produced --- against a mean of $72.6$ CoT tokens on the two that do terminate. That measures nothing about our decode, and we report it as an unaudited row rather than a passing one; the audit script exits non-zero on exactly this state rather than averaging it away. \textbf{We then tested whether that was our token budget or the checkpoint, because the first is our problem and the second is a fact about the model} (compute-platform \texttt{t57wgzya9a}, same audit, $768$ tokens). It is the checkpoint, and the diagnostic is not at the tail but at the head: on $12/12$ frames generation exhausts the doubled budget, and \texttt{think\_start\_first} is $\mathbf{0/12}$ --- the base checkpoint never opens a \texttt{<think>} block at all, emitting runs of \texttt{<action>} (id $257155$) where its two CoT-trained siblings emit reasoning. Upstream's stopping criterion is the two-token tail \texttt{[</think>, <action>]}, so a sequence with no \texttt{<think>} cannot produce one at \emph{any} budget. The comparison is therefore not merely unrun on this checkpoint but undefinable by this method, and we state that rather than leave a raiseable budget implied. One asymmetry keeps it from being fatal and we state it too: the edit protocol \emph{injects} a CoT and never asks a checkpoint to generate one, so the capability \texttt{\_base} lacks is not a capability any published number depends on --- \texttt{build\_input\_cot\_ids} assembles the identical sequence on all three checkpoints and is byte-identical to upstream's own on the two where the comparison exists. What is absent is the confirmation on the third, not a reason to expect it to differ. The scope of the P2 decode-equivalence claim is therefore two architecture families and four of five checkpoints tested, with the fifth named.

We report one thing the same run got wrong, because taken at face value it contradicts the above. The report's \emph{bin-level} agreement is $0$ of $66$ prompts and ${\approx}0$ on all seven dimensions --- and that is the audit's slice, not P2's decode. On $108$ of $108$ decodes (each record's original and edited pass), upstream's span sits exactly one position earlier than P2's: \texttt{bins\_upstream}$[j{+}1]$ equals \texttt{bins\_p2}$[j]$ for $j{=}0\ldots5$ up to upstream's $255{\to}254$ clip, \texttt{bins\_upstream}$[0]$ is the grid top on $108/108$, and \texttt{bins\_p2}$[6]$ is $255$ on $108/108$. The model emits one non-action separator token before the seven action tokens; P2 filters for ids inside the action window and reads $[a_1..a_7]$, while upstream slices a \emph{fixed} \texttt{generated\_\allowbreak{}ids[0,\allowbreak{}-(action\_\allowbreak{}dim+1):-1]} and reads $[\textrm{sep},a_1..a_6]$, putting the separator in dimension $0$ and dropping the gripper. A separator id cannot decode to bin $254$ as an action --- $254$ is what the clip maps it \emph{to} --- which is why dimension $0$ is pinned at the grid top on every decode. So P2's selection is the correct one and the misalignment is a property of \emph{calling} \texttt{predict\_action} with a pre-built \texttt{input\_ids}. It also explains why $\Delta\mathcal{F}$ is exactly $0$ rather than luckily small: the offset is constant across the paired forward passes and the one unshared dimension is saturated in both, so $\Delta_\infty$ is a maximum over the same six varying dimensions either way. The invariance is therefore robust, but it is not the evidence for selection equivalence; the $66/66$ raw-id identity is. The script now measures the offset, releases the raw ids per record so a reader can check the span, and keys its verdict on raw-id identity. The same two upstream-calling-convention bugs --- no \texttt{max\_new\_tokens}, and no handling of the \texttt{(actions,\allowbreak{} generated\_\allowbreak{}ids)} return --- were present in \texttt{anonrepo/\allowbreak{}libero\_\allowbreak{}sim.predict\_\allowbreak{}action\_\allowbreak{}upstream} and are fixed; vanilla OpenVLA's copy of \texttt{predict\_action} sets \texttt{max\_new\_tokens} itself, so the LIBERO rollout path was never affected, which is why this surfaced only on ECoT. That fix is checkable rather than asserted, because the run carries an auxiliary probe that decodes upstream's action from the \emph{instruction-only} prompt and compares it against the CoT prompt: it went from $0$ measurements --- every call raised, which is how the two bugs were found at all --- to $12$ of $12$ samples on which the CoT context changes upstream's own decoded action. We report that as a weak positive and no more: it counts any one of $7$ bins differing, so the bar is low, and $12$ samples support no rate. What it does establish is that the CoT is in the loop under \emph{upstream's} decode method and not only under ours, which is the one thing a reader could otherwise suspect the $66/66$ token identity of concealing. The offset itself is released as a measured field rather than as prose --- \texttt{n\_\allowbreak{}prompts\_\allowbreak{}upstream\_\allowbreak{}slice\_\allowbreak{}offset\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}one} and \texttt{n\_\allowbreak{}prompts\_\allowbreak{}upstream\_\allowbreak{}dim0\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}grid\_\allowbreak{}top} are both $66$ of $66$ prompts, which is the same fact as the $108/108$ above counted per unique prompt instead of per record pass ($12$ originals are shared across the families that edit them).
\paragraph{Norm-stats provenance, and why the rollout-level CoT edit cannot use the public CoT checkpoint.} The de-normalization statistics a checkpoint ships are the one piece of decode provenance we had been taking from filenames rather than from the checkpoint, so we probed it. \texttt{Embodied-CoT/\allowbreak{}ecot-openvla-7b-bridge} carries \texttt{norm\_stats} for exactly one key, \texttt{bridge\_orig}, and no LIBERO key at all: requesting \texttt{libero\_\allowbreak{}spatial\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}noops} raises upstream's own \texttt{ValueError} rather than degrading. That single fact settles two things at once. It is the mechanism behind the withdrawn P3 run above --- there was never a LIBERO percentile set to use, so the only available configuration was the cross-domain one --- and it rules the checkpoint out as the subject of a rollout-level CoT edit, because without LIBERO percentiles its outputs reach \texttt{env.step()} at raw $[-1,1]$ scale and Task SR is pinned at $0$ in \emph{every} arm, unedited control included. Five identically-zero arms are not a null result about CoT faithfulness; they are a broken setup that reads like one. The probe also records what does work, and the two failures are independent: the checkpoint emits a well-formed CoT online on LIBERO frames ($255$ tokens, eight parsed tags, \texttt{cot\_structured} true) and $3$ of the $4$ probed families change the rendered trace, with \emph{subject\_swap} correctly reported inapplicable on that trace rather than scored as a no-effect edit. So the \emph{intervention} half of the rollout protocol transfers and the \emph{action-scale} half does not, which is what re-points the rollout job at our own \mbox{r=32} LIBERO fine-tune: it was trained against raw LIBERO actions clipped to $[-1,1]$, so identity de-quantization \emph{is} its native scale and it consults no \texttt{norm\_stats} on any path. The probe is released with its compute-platform task id (\texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}rollout\_\allowbreak{}probe\_\allowbreak{}ecot\_\allowbreak{}bridge/\allowbreak{}}), and the rollout job reads it as a gate --- it exits rather than spending a $20$-hour slot past a failed precondition, which is the discipline the two silent rollout defects above did not have.

\subsubsection{O4 (observation, not a controlled finding): a Bridge-corpus CoT-VLA is $\sim 2\times$ more faithful, but the comparison confounds two axes}
\label{sec:o4}

Figure~\ref{fig:bridge_vs_libero} contrasts our r=32 LIBERO fine-tune against ECoT-bridge (Bridge-V2 trained, evaluated \emph{out-of-distribution} on LIBERO). On the three shared tier-2/tier-1 families (subject\_swap, direction\_flip, gripper\_flip) ECoT-bridge achieves $\mathcal{F}\!\in\![0.67, 0.97]$ (subject=0.97, direction=0.96, gripper=0.67), roughly $2\text{--}5\times$ our LIBERO r=32 fine-tune's $[0.13, 0.68]$ (subject=0.33, direction=0.68, gripper=0.13). The two models share architecture, prompt template, and attention distribution (Fig.~\ref{fig:attention}, difference $<0.01$).

\textbf{We deliberately do \emph{not} promote this contrast to a numbered finding.} The comparison confounds at least two axes: (i) the public ECoT-bridge model was trained on a substantially larger corpus (Bridge-V2, $\sim60$k trajectories vs LIBERO-90, $\sim4$k trajectories in our fine-tune, a $15\times$ data-quantity gap); (ii) the reasoning-trace distribution at training time also differs (Bridge-V2 CoT annotations vs LIBERO-90 CoT annotations). A same-data ablation -- fine-tuning ECoT-bridge on a downsampled $\sim4$k-trajectory Bridge subset matched to LIBERO-90, or upsampling LIBERO to Bridge scale, then re-reporting -- would be needed before this observation could support a causal claim about either axis alone. We mark that ablation ($\sim 1$--$2$ GPU-days) as future work and report O4 here only as a motivating \emph{observation}, not as a controlled finding at the level of F1/F2/F3.

\paragraph{The blocker on that ablation is not compute, and we measured what it is.}
Running it requires the Bridge~V2 CoT annotations joined to the trajectories per episode, and the two public artifacts that carry them share no such key. We measured all three candidates on the full exports (compute-platform \texttt{754ru9usqe}, CPU-only; released as \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}bridge\_\allowbreak{}join\_\allowbreak{}probe/\allowbreak{}}). The annotations' own \texttt{episode\_id} matches only $1{,}111$ of $53{,}192$ LeRobot episodes ($2.1\%$); its range is $[0,1110]$ against $60{,}062$ annotated episodes, so it numbers episodes within a shard rather than globally; it collides $879$ times; and on the pairs it does match, the two sides' language instructions agree only $0.280$ of the time. That last number is the one that matters, because a join on \texttt{episode\_id} fails \emph{invisibly}: it returns a complete, plausible index, a training run on it completes normally, and the resulting checkpoint cannot be distinguished post hoc from one trained on a correct index. The LeRobot episode records carry only \texttt{episode\_index}, \texttt{length} and \texttt{tasks}, so no exact route exists either. What remains is the instruction text: $19{,}541$ shared normalized instructions cover $38{,}660$ of $53{,}192$ LeRobot episodes ($72.7\%$) at a median fanout of $1$, giving $41{,}634$ reachable annotated episodes --- an order of magnitude more than the ablation needs, but \emph{task}-level rather than trajectory-level wherever the fanout exceeds one, and requiring that degenerate keys be refused rather than sampled within (the shared keys include crowdsourced strings that are not language, and the maximum fanout on a single key is $963$). Separately, a correct join is still not a renderable trace: this export splits the eight CoT tags across its \texttt{features} and \texttt{reasoning} subtrees, and over $4{,}000$ inspected steps \texttt{reasoning} alone fills six of eight tags and leaves VISIBLE OBJECTS and GRIPPER POSITION at $0.0$, so a trainer that renders from it alone --- as ours did --- would train the model to emit two permanently blank tags, which no metric in this benchmark can detect. We report this because O4 is the one place where we ask the reader to accept an uncontrolled comparison, and the reason the control is missing is a property of the public data rather than a budget we declined to spend. \textbf{O4 (observation): under uncontrolled training-regime differences (data quantity $\times$ target-corpus distribution), a Bridge-trained CoT-VLA and our LIBERO fine-tune differ by $\sim 2\times$ in Faithfulness Score while sharing architecture and attention distribution; no single axis can be credited from this comparison.}

\subsubsection{F5: attention profile and causal-edit response are cross-corpus consistent (N=100 per non-LIBERO corpus)}
\label{sec:cross_corpus}

We ran the ECoT-bridge model on 3 additional manipulation corpora spanning distinct embodiments: Bridge~V2 (WidowX bimanual home, $N{=}100$), RT-1/Fractal (Google office robot, $N{=}100$), BC-Z (everyday manipulation, $N{=}100$). Because these corpora do not carry ground-truth CoT annotations, we let the model self-generate its 9-tag CoT via greedy decode, then apply the same edit protocol. These runs replace an $N{=}30$ pilot, and the replacement is the reason the transfer claim is now worth making: \textbf{every attention bucket mean moves by at most $0.3$\,pp between the two $N$}, so the stability was not a small-sample artifact. The pilot is retained under \texttt{results\_v2/superseded/}.

\textbf{Attention profile is remarkably stable across corpora.} Per-corpus $(\text{visual}, \text{instr}, \text{cot}, \text{prev})$ mean$\pm$std, $N{=}100$ everywhere (BC-Z contributes $99$ usable attention records of its $100$ samples): LIBERO $(.290, .301, .343, .065)$ $\pm(.006, .009, .009, .002)$; Bridge~V2 $(.296, .299, .338, .067)$ $\pm(.010, .012, .017, .004)$; Fractal $(.291, .302, .335, .073)$ $\pm(.008, .010, .014, .004)$; BC-Z $(.297, .310, .323, .070)$ $\pm(.010, .014, .022, .004)$. \textbf{Max deviation across corpora is $\leq 2.1$\,pp on any bucket} --- BC-Z's CoT bucket, $2.07$\,pp below LIBERO's, is the largest --- \textbf{and every other bucket on every corpus is within $0.9$\,pp.} The LIBERO reference row is the 3-seed \emph{ecot-bridge} profile the rest of the paper uses, so this table and Section~\ref{sec:results} cannot disagree.

\textbf{Causal-edit response also transfers, and at this $N$ the spread narrows.} On direction\_flip: LIBERO $\mathcal{F}\!=\!0.963$ ($N{=}100$), Bridge~V2 $0.913$ ($N{=}92$), Fractal $0.974$ ($N{=}77$), BC-Z $0.951$ ($N{=}81$) --- a range of $0.06$ across four corpora, where the $N{=}30$ pilot's $1.00$/$0.92$/$0.92$ spanned $0.08$ on $N{=}25$--$26$ apiece. On gripper\_flip: LIBERO $0.697$, Bridge~V2 $0.804$ ($N{=}51$), Fractal $0.770$ ($N{=}74$), BC-Z $0.746$ ($N{=}63$). The per-family $N$ is what the visibility gate admits, and it is $2$--$4\times$ the pilot's on every cell. \textbf{F5: Both the attention profile and the primary causal-edit responses of a CoT-VLA transfer cross-corpus at $N{=}100$; CoT-Faith metrics can serve as portable diagnostics across embodiments.} What F5 does \emph{not} say, and Section~\ref{app:sec:directional} makes explicit: these are \emph{magnitude} responses, and it is exactly the magnitude score that Section~\ref{sec:f2_calib} shows is uninterpretable without its floor. The nulls were not run on these corpora, so F5 is a portability result for the \emph{pipeline}, not evidence that the CoT drives the action on any of them.

\subsubsection{F6: magnitude-based edit scoring inverts the model ordering}
\label{app:sec:directional}

Eq.~\ref{app:eq:delta} scores an edit by the \emph{magnitude} $\Delta_\infty$ of the action change, so a model is credited as ``faithful'' for changing its action in \emph{any} direction after the CoT is edited. For families whose semantics predict a \emph{signed} consequence this is too weak a test. After \emph{direction\_flip} reverses left$\leftrightarrow$right / up$\leftrightarrow$down / in$\leftrightarrow$out, a model that understood the edit should move roughly opposite to its original translation; after \emph{gripper\_flip} it should invert the gripper sign; after \emph{negation} it should shrink its action norm. We therefore define a direction-aware score. For \emph{direction\_flip},
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}(m, f) &\;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{s=1}^{N} \mathbf{1}\!\left[c^f_s < -0.5\right],\\
c^f_s &\;=\; \cos\bigl(a_{1:3}(s, \text{cot}_s),\, a_{1:3}(s, f(\text{cot}_s))\bigr)
\end{aligned}
\label{app:eq:fdir}
\end{equation}
with the analogous sign-flip criterion on dimension 7 for \emph{gripper\_flip} and a norm-shrinkage criterion for \emph{negation}. This requires no new inference: it is computed from the per-sample $a_{\text{orig}}, a_{\text{edit}}$ pairs we already release.

\textbf{The ranking reverses.} Table~\ref{tab:directional} reports both scores on \emph{direction\_flip}. ECoT-bridge --- numerically highest in every magnitude column of Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} --- has $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}{=}0.963 \pm 0.006$ but $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}{=}0.120 \pm 0.043$ across 3 seeds, and its mean translation cosine is $+0.415 \pm 0.055$: \textbf{it moves in substantially the \emph{same} direction after the direction is reversed}. The LoRA variants it outscores by $1.2\text{--}1.5\times$ on magnitude genuinely reverse ($\cos = -0.111$ to $-0.509$ over all six; $-0.74$ to $-0.89$ on the subset that magnitude-scoring counts as faithful) and therefore outscore ECoT-bridge by $4.5\text{--}6.5\times$ on $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$. The magnitude ordering of the eight models is not merely compressed under direction-aware scoring --- it is close to inverted, and the inversion is far larger than the seed noise that produces it: ECoT-bridge's $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ deficit against r=64 is $0.659$ against per-row seed stds of $0.043$ and $0.021$. This is the concrete reason Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} carries no bolded winner: the two scoring rules disagree about who is best, so publishing either as \emph{the} ranking would be a choice of conclusion rather than a measurement.

\emph{gripper\_flip} is worse still: $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}} \leq 0.03$ for \emph{every} model, and \textbf{exactly $0.000$ across all three seeds on ECoT-bridge}, with $\cos$ between $+0.93$ and $+1.00$ throughout, i.e.\ no model in the cohort ever reliably inverts its gripper command when the CoT tells it to.

\paragraph{$\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$, unlike $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$, has a null it clears --- and it correctly fails the no-CoT control.} Our own criticism of the field is that an instrument reported without a null cannot distinguish a real reading from a generic response to perturbation, and $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ was introduced above without one. We therefore calibrate it against the same families that sink $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ (\texttt{scripts/fdir\_null.py}). A non-directional edit has no reason to invert the translation vector, so \emph{paraphrase\_null}, \emph{syntactic\_scramble}, \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null}, \emph{cross\_task\_swap}, \emph{verb\_swap}, \emph{negation}, \emph{subject\_swap} and \emph{instr\_random\_sub} jointly define the floor, and we take the \emph{ceiling} over all eight as the null rather than any single one.

\textbf{On the six CoT-trained LoRA and data variants \emph{direction\_flip} clears that ceiling by $6.2$--$11.1\times$} --- r=64 at $0.779$ against a null ceiling of $0.070$, r=32 at $0.589$ against $0.077$ --- \textbf{while the no-CoT control sits \emph{below} its own floor} ($0.087$ against $0.113$, the one configuration where the treatment does not clear the null). That is the behaviour a calibrated instrument should show and the exact behaviour $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ fails to show: on the same no-CoT control $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ reads $0.187$ over the semantic families and is indistinguishable from its $0.193$ paraphrase floor, so magnitude scoring cannot tell the ablation apart from the models it ablates, and the direction check can. ECoT-bridge clears at $3.8\times$ ($0.150$ vs $0.040$) --- a real margin on a small absolute number, which is the same result as Table~\ref{tab:directional}'s $0.96 \to 0.12$ collapse seen from the null side. All three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints return $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}} \leq 0.010$ at floors of $0.000$--$0.050$ and do \emph{not} clear, so the second architecture family fails the direction check outright rather than passing it weakly; we report that as a negative row, not as coverage. \textbf{$7$ of $11$ configurations clear their own null.} We state this as the constructive half of the paper: a direction-aware score with a measured, per-model floor is the instrument we can defend, and it is what the admission rule should be built on --- not $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$, whose floor question Section~\ref{sec:paraphrase_null} shows to be unanswerable in either direction.

\textbf{F6: Magnitude-based CoT-edit protocols rank \emph{brittleness}, not directional understanding, and can order models exactly backwards.} We regard this as the most consequential methodological result in the paper, and it applies beyond CoT-Faith: the driving-VLA CoT-intervention protocols we build on \citep{vladrivebench,pinocchio} score edits by action change magnitude and inherit the same failure. We therefore report $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ alongside $\mathcal{F}$ for every signed family, and recommend that a magnitude-only faithfulness number never be reported alone.



Figure~\ref{fig:ablation} isolates two additional axes. Panel (a) shows the LoRA rank sweep ($r \in \{8, 16, 64\}$) on 5 edit families. Higher rank monotonically raises faithful rate on cross\_task\_swap ($0.86 \to 0.94$) and verb\_swap ($0.70 \to 0.84$); gripper\_flip is rank-insensitive. Panel (b) shows two 50\%-data seeds (A and B): seed-level variance is $\leq 15$pp on all 5 families, confirming that our main-result gaps (no-CoT collapse, Bridge vs LIBERO) are not artifacts of a single data split.

\subsubsection{Paraphrase-null: models are sensitive to surface tokens, not just meaning}
\label{sec:paraphrase_null}

The identity-substitution \emph{selfsplice\_control} ($\mathcal{F}\!=\!0.00$ on 8/8 models) validates only that the tokenizer is deterministic; a byte-identical string produces a byte-identical action by construction, so this null cannot fire on any model. To strengthen the null we introduce \emph{paraphrase\_null}: verb synonyms that preserve directions, objects, and arguments (\textit{move}$\to$\textit{shift}, \textit{grasp}$\to$\textit{seize}, \textit{turn}$\to$\textit{rotate}, etc.\ --- 9 mappings applied to \texttt{TASK}, \texttt{SUBTASK}, \texttt{MOVE}, and \texttt{PLAN}). A model faithful to \emph{semantic content} should show $\mathcal{F}\!\approx\!0$ under this edit; a model faithful only to surface tokens would show $\mathcal{F}\!>\!0$.

\textbf{Result on ECoT-bridge (3 seeds, $N{=}100$ each): $\mathcal{F}(\text{paraphrase\_null}) = 0.95 \pm 0.02$.} The model changes its action for $\geq 95\%$ of meaning-preserving edits. We initially read this as a substantive finding about surface-form sensitivity. It is more than that, and the stronger reading is unfavourable to the metric: \textbf{$\mathcal{F}(\text{paraphrase\_null}) = 0.947$ is statistically indistinguishable from $\mathcal{F}(\text{cross\_task\_swap}) = 0.963 \pm 0.012$}, the family we declared the \emph{maximum}-effect control (replacing the entire trace with an unrelated task's reasoning), and from \emph{direction\_flip} $0.963$, \emph{verb\_swap} $0.950$ and \emph{negation} $0.947$. Normalized by the model's own ceiling, $\mathcal{F}(\text{paraphrase\_null})/\mathcal{F}(\text{cross\_task\_swap}) = 0.98$. A metric that cannot separate ``\emph{move}$\to$\emph{shift}'' from ``replace the whole trace'' is not, on its own, measuring CoT$\to$action \emph{semantic} causal flow. The two paragraphs after next narrow \emph{what} it is measuring instead, using two further floors: it is not brittleness to \emph{any} perturbation (a numeric one scores $0.46$), but it is also not specific to the CoT (an out-of-CoT control scores $0.99$).

\paragraph{Differential Faithfulness Score.} We therefore report a floor-corrected statistic as the primary number,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}(m, f) \;=\; \mathcal{F}(m, f) \;-\; \mathcal{F}(m, \text{paraphrase\_null}),
\label{eq:fdiff}
\end{equation}
which asks how much of a family's response exceeds that model's own surface-form floor. On ECoT-bridge the consequence is stark: $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}} = -0.087$, i.e.\ \textbf{the flagship model's mean faithfulness sits \emph{below} its own paraphrase floor}. (This pairs the 3-seed 11-family runs, floor $0.947$; the independent single-seed 13-family calibration run reported in the next two paragraphs pairs floor $0.960$ against $\bar{\mathcal{F}} = 0.869$ and gives $-0.091$. Both are negative; we quote the 13-family value wherever the three floors are compared, since only that run measures all three under one configuration.) Per family, $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ is $\approx 0$ on most families ($+0.017$ cross\_task\_swap, $+0.016$ direction\_flip, $-0.014$ adversarial\_plausible) and clearly negative on \emph{gripper\_flip} ($0.697 - 0.947 = -0.250$) and \emph{location\_swap} ($0.594 - 0.947 = -0.353$). We state the implication plainly rather than burying it: \emph{on ECoT-bridge, CoT-Faith's magnitude score detects almost no semantic sensitivity above the surface-form floor}, and the honest headline for this model is a null result, not a $0.86$ faithfulness score. Section~\ref{app:sec:directional} shows the same conclusion from an independent direction.

\paragraph{Second calibration floor: the metric \emph{does} discriminate.} A single floor family could itself be anomalous, so we ran a second: \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null}, which perturbs the \texttt{VISIBLE OBJECTS} bounding-box coordinates by $\pm 1$\,px --- below the resolution the reasoning operates at, and therefore meaning-preserving in the same sense as a synonym swap. \textbf{It scores $\mathcal{F} = 0.46$ ($N{=}100$), less than half the paraphrase floor}, and $\bar{\mathcal{F}} - \mathcal{F}(\text{bbox\_jitter\_null}) = +0.409$. This is a genuine positive for the metric and we report it as such: $\mathcal{F}$ is \emph{not} pure decode brittleness, because a real meaning-preserving perturbation exists that it correctly ignores more than half the time. The correct diagnosis is narrower than ``the metric measures nothing'': \emph{lexical} perturbation anywhere in the reasoning saturates it, while \emph{numeric} perturbation does not.

\paragraph{Third floor, out-of-CoT: the response is not CoT-specific.} The sharpest test is a perturbation that is not in the CoT at all. \emph{instr\_random\_sub} substitutes 5 random tokens in the \emph{instruction}, leaving the reasoning untouched, and so upper-bounds how much of any CoT-edit score can be attributed to CoT$\to$action routing rather than to generic prompt sensitivity. \textbf{It scores $\mathcal{F} = 0.99$ ($N{=}99$) --- higher than every one of the ten CoT edit families, including \emph{cross\_task\_swap}.} Zero of the seven non-control CoT families reach it; the ratio $\bar{\mathcal{F}} / \mathcal{F}(\text{instr\_random\_sub}) = 0.878$, i.e.\ editing the model's own reasoning moves its action \emph{less} reliably than randomly corrupting five instruction tokens. We take this as the decisive construct-validity result of the paper: \textbf{on ECoT-bridge, no part of the CoT-edit response requires the CoT-editing hypothesis, because a control that never touches the CoT explains all of it and more}. Any claim of the form ``model $m$ scores $\mathcal{F}$ on CoT edits, therefore its reasoning is causally load-bearing'' must first show $\mathcal{F}(\text{CoT edit}) > \mathcal{F}(\text{out-of-CoT control})$ for that model. Ours does not. We therefore make \emph{instr\_random\_sub} a required-reporting family for every leaderboard submission, and Section~\ref{sec:f2_calib} states the corresponding restriction on F2.

\paragraph{Is the floor itself confounded with sequence length? Yes --- and swapping it does not rescue the metric, it inverts the sign.} \emph{paraphrase\_null} is the one family in the taxonomy that changes token count: its synonym table contains multi-word expansions (\textit{release}$\to$``let go of'', \textit{open}$\to$``unclose''), and measured over the $437$ judged pairs it changes word count on $38/40$ heads by a mean of $+0.97$ words, while \emph{direction\_flip}, \emph{negation}, \emph{syntactic\_scramble} and \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} change it on $0/40$. The semantic families $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ subtracts the floor \emph{from} are length-exact; the floor is not. A reviewer is therefore right to ask whether Eq.~\ref{eq:fdiff} subtracts a length perturbation rather than a semantic no-op, and we did not test this before submission.

The test is available on disk, because the taxonomy already contains a second meaning-preserving family that is length-exact by construction. \emph{syntactic\_scramble} reorders clauses without substituting words; the same blind judge that scores \emph{paraphrase\_null} at $\text{meaning\_preserved}=0.975$ scores it at $1.000$. Recomputing $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ against it, over all twelve configurations (\texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}floor\_\allowbreak{}invariance.py}), gives the result we least expected and must report: \textbf{$\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ is negative on $12/12$ against \emph{paraphrase\_null} and positive on $12/12$ against \emph{syntactic\_scramble}. The sign flips on every single configuration.}

That does not mean the length-exact floor is the right one and the headline should be reversed. It means something worse for the instrument, and it is the finding we now lead this section with: \textbf{on $12/12$ configurations the gap between the two floors exceeds the gap between the semantic mean and \emph{either} floor}. On our r=32 fine-tune the two meaning-preserving families sit at $0.567$ and $0.348$ --- a spread of $0.219$ --- while the semantic mean $0.438$ lies \emph{between} them, $0.129$ from one and $0.090$ from the other. Two edits that the judge certifies mean the same thing disagree with each other more than either disagrees with edits that change the meaning. Under those conditions no choice of meaning-preserving floor licenses a claim about semantic content, and reporting $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ against \emph{syntactic\_scramble} instead would be trading one unlicensed sign for its opposite. \textbf{We therefore report both floors everywhere and treat the magnitude metric as uninformative about meaning in either direction} --- a weaker claim than our submitted one, and the one the data supports. What survives this is not $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ at all but the direction check of Section~\ref{app:sec:directional}, which is the only instrument here with a null it clears.

\paragraph{All eleven calibrated models, in both architecture families: the degeneracy tracks saturation, and the specificity check splits.} A construct-validity failure measured on one checkpoint could be a defect of the protocol or a property of that checkpoint. The submission separated the two on a single second model; we have since run the identical 13-family protocol on \emph{every} model in the benchmark --- at 3 sampling seeds each for the seven leaderboard checkpoints, and including the three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints of Section~\ref{sec:cross_family}, whose reasoning format, backbone and action decode are all different --- which turns Table~\ref{tab:calibration} from two rows into twelve and changes what can be concluded from it in three distinct directions, one of which is favourable to the metric and was invisible at $n{=}2$. The twelve rows are eleven distinct checkpoints: \emph{Ours no-CoT} appears twice by design, once as the checkpoint every other table uses and once as an independent retraining of the same configuration.

\emph{First, the degeneracy is saturation and nothing else --- and it now says so once per architecture family.} Exactly $\mathbf{2}$ of the $12$ calibrations are degenerate, and they are the two \emph{saturated} checkpoints: ECoT-bridge at a range of $0.010$ and DeepThinkVLA-base at $0.020$. Every other row spans $0.067$ to $0.337$, up to $34\times$ wider. Both degenerate rows are public checkpoints that were never fine-tuned toward the evaluation suite, one in each architecture family, and \emph{no} full-CoT trained variant is degenerate in either family. So \textbf{the collapse of a calibration is a property of \emph{saturation}, not of the edit families or of one CoT format}, and that now rests on ten contrasting models across two architectures rather than on eight within one. This sharpens finding (a) considerably: $\mathcal{F}$ is not uninterpretable everywhere, it is uninterpretable \emph{where it is high} --- exactly the regime in which anyone would want to cite it as evidence of faithfulness. A floor near zero and a ceiling at $0.22$ leave room to measure something; a floor at $0.960$ against a ceiling of $0.970$ does not.

\emph{Second, the central negative result generalizes across architectures, and it is not a saturation artifact.} On $\mathbf{11}$ of $\mathbf{12}$ entries $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ sits \emph{below} that model's own paraphrase floor ($\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ from $-0.179$ to $+0.014$), and the two-sided statistic $(\bar{\mathcal{F}} - \text{floor})/(\text{ceiling} - \text{floor})$ is \emph{negative} on $\mathbf{9}$ of the $10$ entries where it is defined at all --- including \textbf{all eight non-degenerate full-CoT variants, in both architecture families}, whose floors sit at $0.45$--$0.82$ and are nowhere near ceiling. This is the result the submission could state for one checkpoint and had to leave as a question everywhere else, and the DeepThinkVLA pair is what turns it from a claim about one CoT format into a claim about CoT-VLAs: \textbf{a meaning-preserving synonym swap moves the action more reliably than a semantic edit does, on every full-CoT model we have measured}. The one positive is \emph{ours-no-CoT (replicate)} at $+0.127$, and it is the model that was trained on an action-only target and therefore \emph{should} return approximately its own floor; we report it as the protocol's one clean positive control at the model level. Its leaderboard sibling returns $-0.416$ from the same configuration, which is why item~(viii) exists.

\emph{Third --- and this is the one direction in which more models made the metric look better --- the out-of-CoT control is not universally decisive.} On ECoT-bridge the specificity ratio is $0.878$ and we called it the decisive construct-validity result of the paper. That statement was true of that checkpoint and is \emph{not} true in general: the ratio exceeds $1$ on $\mathbf{5}$ of the $12$ entries. We report the correction rather than keeping the stronger claim. But the margins are small in the only units that matter. Every trained configuration has now been trained a second time, and retraining moves $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ itself by $0.006$--$\mathbf{0.092}$ across those seven pairs; \textbf{none of the five entries that clear the out-of-CoT control clears it by more than the largest of those}. \emph{data-50B} ($+0.083$) and \emph{r=8} ($+0.074$) come closest and still fall under it, \emph{r=32} ($+0.025$), \emph{r=64} ($+0.014$) and \emph{r=16} ($+0.009$) are well inside it, and the pair that moves $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ by the full $0.092$ is \emph{data-50B}'s own --- the entry with the widest margin. Per family the picture is the same: on those five entries only $3$ or $4$ of the $7$ non-control families individually reach the control. And the second architecture family does not clear it \emph{at all}: the ratio is $0.996$, $0.806$ and $0.814$ on DeepThinkVLA-base, -SFT and -RL, so all $5$ entries above $1$ are ECoT variants trained by us. So the honest summary is narrower than either the submission's claim or its opposite: \emph{no model in this benchmark clears its own out-of-CoT control by a margin that survives its own training-run variance}, and \emph{instr\_random\_sub} therefore stays a required-reporting family (Section~\ref{sec:f2_calib}) rather than a check that has now been passed.

\emph{Fourth, the numeric floor is near zero everywhere it applies except the saturated model.} \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} scores $0.047$--$0.087$ on the eight trained ECoT variants against $0.460$ on ECoT-bridge. The ``lexical perturbation saturates it, numeric perturbation does not'' diagnosis therefore holds across that family and is sharper than the ECoT-bridge number alone suggested: on the models that are not saturated, $\mathcal{F}$ correctly ignores a meaning-preserving numeric perturbation more than $91\%$ of the time. This is the one calibration column that does \emph{not} extend to the second architecture family, and the reason is structural rather than a gap in our runs: DeepThinkVLA renders no bounding boxes, so there is no numeric field in its CoT to jitter. We record that as $n{=}0$ with $100$ skipped and decline to report the $\mathcal{F}=0.000$ an unguarded run produces --- which, before the harness was fixed, is exactly what our own committed artifacts contained for these three checkpoints, at $n{=}100$ with every $\Delta$ identically zero. A vacuous edit scored as perfect robustness is the most flattering kind of measurement error, and it is why the harness now refuses to score an edit that does not survive rendering.

Each row's floors, ceiling and $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ come from one 3-seed 13-family run for that model (\texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}ours\_\allowbreak{}*\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}13family\_\allowbreak{}seed\{\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}2\}.json}; ECoT-bridge from \texttt{ecot\_\allowbreak{}bridge\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}13family\_\allowbreak{}calibration.json}, the no-CoT replicate from \texttt{ours\_\allowbreak{}no-cot\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}13family\_\allowbreak{}calibration.json}, and the three DeepThinkVLA rows from \texttt{deepthink\_\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}base,\allowbreak{}sft,\allowbreak{}rl\}\_\allowbreak{}13family.json}), so every comparison within a row is within a single configuration. Seed~0 of each new ``ours'' run reproduces the superseded single-seed run \emph{bit-exactly} on $9$ of its $10$ families; the tenth is \emph{location\_swap}, which moves only because these runs postdate the C5 annotation fix and score it at $N\!\approx\!74$ instead of $N{=}12$. The three DeepThinkVLA rows are a different architecture and are compared only against their own in-run floor and ceiling, never against the ECoT rows; they are the same runs Section~\ref{sec:cross_family} reports, so that section's table and this one cannot disagree.

\subsubsection{Do the edit families do what their names say? An LLM-judge validation of the generators}
\label{sec:judge_edits}

Every result in this paper is conditional on a set of claims we had asserted from generator source code and never measured: that \emph{paraphrase\_null} preserves meaning, that \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} perturbs a number without touching semantics, that \emph{adversarial\_plausible} substitutes an object that stays visually plausible. These are not decorative. $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ is a floor-corrected statistic \emph{only} if the floor family really is meaning-preserving, so the central negative result of Sections~\ref{sec:f2_calib} and~\ref{sec:paraphrase_null} --- $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ below the paraphrase floor on $11$ of $12$ calibrations --- rests on a premise that had the same evidential status as the caveats this revision has been replacing with measurements. So we measured it.

\paragraph{Protocol.} An independent LLM judge (\texttt{Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct}, neither of the architecture families under test) reads each $(\text{original}, \text{edited})$ reasoning pair and answers four binary questions --- meaning preserved, same referent, same direction, still plausible --- plus a $1$--$5$ fluency rating. It is blind to which family produced the pair and never sees the model's action. $480$ pairs were constructed over $40$ samples $\times$ $11$ families plus an identity control; $437$ were judged and all $43$ skips are itemized, every one of them a case where the \emph{generator} found no applicable edit ($16$ \emph{adversarial\_plausible}, $16$ \emph{subject\_swap}, $10$ \emph{location\_swap}) plus one identical render.

\paragraph{The judge is itself gated, on three checks, before any of its rates are read.} A judge that answers ``preserved'' unconditionally would validate every null in the paper, so the identity check alone is not enough. (a) \emph{Identity control}: on $40$ pairs where the edit is $X \to X$, preserved rate $= \mathbf{1.000}$. (b) \emph{Negative control}: pooled over the families designed to destroy meaning, preserved rate $= \mathbf{0.175}$, which is what rules out the degenerate judge the first gate would pass. (c) \emph{Order agreement}: presenting the two traces in the opposite order changes the verdict on $77$ of $437$ pairs, so agreement is $\mathbf{0.824}$ --- a real presentation bias, and the noise floor to attach to every rate below. All three pass and the run is marked valid.

\paragraph{Three of four declared premises hold; the fourth fails.} \emph{paraphrase\_null} preserves meaning at $0.975$ (fluency $4.92$) and \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} at $1.000$ (fluency $5.00$). \textbf{The two nulls that $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ and the numeric-floor argument depend on are validated}, which is the outcome those arguments needed and did not previously have. \emph{syntactic\_scramble} also comes back at $1.000$. But \emph{adversarial\_plausible} fails: the referent changes on $0.958$ of pairs, as designed, while only $\mathbf{0.125}$ of its edits are judged plausible against a taxonomy entry that called them ``visually plausible but wrong''. Counting the $16$ samples where the generator produced no edit at all, the family delivers a plausible substitution on $3$ of $40$ attempts. \textbf{The ``second-most visible object'' heuristic does not produce plausible substitutions}, so \emph{adversarial\_plausible} has been measuring an unconstrained object swap, which is a weaker intervention than its name claims and one that overlaps \emph{subject\_swap} more than we intended. We do not delete the family or its numbers --- its $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ ($-0.014$ on ECoT-bridge) are unaffected by what the edit is \emph{called} --- we correct the description, in Section~\ref{sec:taxonomy} and here. No claim in this paper turns on the plausibility of that family; had one done so, this measurement would have withdrawn it.

\paragraph{Two findings we were not looking for.} First, \emph{syntactic\_scramble} at a preserved rate of $1.000$ is a \emph{third} meaning-preserving family, and it is listed in Tier~0 as a structural edit. Its $\mathcal{F}$ is therefore a second within-CoT surface-form floor, independent of \emph{paraphrase\_null}'s lexical route to the same thing --- which strengthens rather than weakens Section~\ref{sec:paraphrase_null}: two unrelated ways of preserving meaning both move the action. Second, \emph{verb\_swap} changes meaning on only $0.575$ of pairs and direction on $0.350$, so roughly $4$ in $10$ ``verb swaps'' are not semantic edits. \textbf{This is the same family that carries the largest same-config retraining movement in the benchmark} ($\max|\Delta\mathcal{F}| = 0.260$ on $r{=}8$, worst family on $3$ of the $7$ pairs, item~(viii)): the least semantically reliable generator is also the noisiest cell, and we now think those two facts are the same fact. The families with no declared premise behave as intended --- \emph{cross\_task\_swap} preserves meaning on $0.025$, \emph{gripper\_flip} on $0.050$, \emph{negation} on $0.100$, and \emph{direction\_flip} on $0.200$ while holding the referent at $1.000$ and changing the direction on all $40$.

\paragraph{What this does not establish.} The judge validates the \emph{generators}, not the specific pairs that produced any published number. The released edit records store actions only, and demo/step identity is not recoverable without re-iterating the $17$\,GB tfds shards, so the judge re-runs the same generators over the same reasoning corpus restricted to the demo files the scored run drew from. It is also one judge model at $n{=}40$ per family, with a measured $17.6\%$ order-flip rate, so these rates should be read to two decimal places at most. Artifact \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}judge\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}families/\allowbreak{}} carries the report, all $437$ judged pairs with both traces verbatim, and its compute-platform task id.

\subsubsection{F7: P2 on a second architecture family --- the construct-validity failure replicates, and worsens}
\label{sec:cross_family}

Every causal-edit result above came from one architecture family. That was the single largest threat to the leaderboard's external validity: a protocol calibrated on ECoT-style nine-tag reasoning over an OpenVLA backbone might measure a property of that stack rather than of CoT-VLAs. We now run the full 13-family protocol on the three public DeepThinkVLA checkpoints --- a PaliGemma model initialized from \texttt{pi0fast\_base}, with a single \texttt{<think>} block instead of nine tags, and a hybrid causal/bidirectional decoder that emits a $(10,7)$ action chunk in one forward pass rather than one autoregressive $7$-vector. Architecturally, reasoning format, and decode are all different. All three runs decoded $100/100$ observations with zero failures, and score $12$ of the $13$ families; the thirteenth, \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null}, is inapplicable to this architecture rather than unmeasured (\S~\ref{sec:f2_calib}), so these are the same runs Table~\ref{tab:calibration} reports and the two tables cannot disagree.

The critical property of these runs is that they carry \emph{paraphrase\_null} (floor) and \emph{cross\_task\_swap} (ceiling) in the same run as the semantic families, so $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ and the two-sided normalization are defined here exactly as in Section~\ref{sec:f2_calib}, computed by the same code path. Table~\ref{tab:crossfamily} reports them.

Three results, in increasing order of how badly they hurt. All three are stated on a scoring convention that we must declare before they can be read, because it is a choice and not a neutral default.

\paragraph{Which of the seventy emitted numbers is scored, and what happens on the other sixty-nine.} DeepThinkVLA emits a $(10,7)$ action chunk in one forward pass, where ECoT emits a single $7$-vector. We score $\Delta_\infty$ on chunk step $0$, which is the step comparable to what the ECoT models emit, and the harness records the chunk-wide $\Delta_\infty$ beside it on every record (\texttt{delta\_linf\_chunk}). \textbf{Earlier versions of this paper stated neither the choice nor its consequence, which is a material omission because the two conventions do not agree.} Scored over the full $(10,7)$ chunk instead, all three checkpoints go to $\mathcal{F}(\text{paraphrase\_null}) = 1.000$ --- every sample --- and $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ becomes $1.000$ / $0.993$ / $0.994$ on base / SFT / RL, so the floor-to-ceiling range that distinguishes the two CoT-tuned rows from the degenerate base row collapses to $0.000$ / $0.000$ / $-0.010$ and \emph{all three} rows become degenerate. Both columns are in the release and either can be recomputed from the same records.

We keep step $0$ as the primary because it is the only convention under which the DeepThinkVLA and ECoT rows measure the same event, and a cross-architecture replication scored two different ways is not a replication. But the honest statement of what the chunk column does to result (2) below is this: \textbf{under the full-chunk convention the second architecture family is saturated end-to-end, and the claim that degeneracy localizes to the saturated public checkpoints rather than to the protocol holds only under the step-$0$ convention.} That weakens result (2) specifically. It leaves result (1) standing on the two CoT-tuned checkpoints, where $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ is negative under \emph{both} conventions ($-0.062$ and $-0.053$ at step $0$; $-0.007$ and $-0.006$ over the chunk); on the base checkpoint the chunk convention drives $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ to exactly $0.000$ with floor and mean both saturated at $1.000$, which is not a negative reading but an undefined one, and we count it as such rather than as support.

\emph{(1) The construct-validity failure is not architecture-specific.} $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ is negative on all three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints, as it is on ECoT-bridge: $4$ of the $4$ models for which we have a measured floor score \emph{below} their own paraphrase null. This is the check that would have dissolved the finding had it come out the other way, run on the family least likely to share ECoT's failure mode, and it replicates.

\emph{(2) On the base checkpoint the calibration is degenerate in the same way ECoT-bridge's is.} Floor $0.960$ against ceiling $0.980$ is a dynamic range of $0.020$, below our $0.05$ threshold, so the two-sided statistic is undefined --- the identical pathology to ECoT-bridge's $0.960/0.970$, reached from a completely different architecture and reasoning format. The two CoT-tuned checkpoints do have a real range ($0.150$, $0.120$), and there the two-sided score is \emph{negative} ($-0.80$ SFT, $-0.91$ RL) because $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ sits below the floor. We flag rather than quote those numbers: a negative normalized score is not ``low faithfulness'', it is the absence of a signal to normalize.

\emph{(3) The direction-aware collapse is much sharper here than on ECoT.} On \emph{direction\_flip}, magnitude $\mathcal{F}$ reads $0.970$ / $0.650$ / $0.640$ (base / SFT / RL) while $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ reads $0.000$ / $0.010$ / $0.010$. Reversing every directional term in the CoT changes the action almost always and reverses it essentially \emph{never} --- at most $1$ sample in $100$ on any of the three. Section~\ref{app:sec:directional} reported $0.963 \to 0.120$ for ECoT-bridge; the same dissociation on this family is $0.970 \to 0.000$. \emph{gripper\_flip} behaves the same way ($0.830/0.430/0.540$ magnitude versus $0.000/0.100/0.060$ direction-aware). Whatever these models do with an edited CoT, it is not following it.

One positive control passes cleanly and is worth stating because it constrains the above: \emph{selfsplice\_control}, which replaces the CoT with a verbatim copy of itself, yields $\mathcal{F} = 0.000$ exactly on all three checkpoints ($\Delta_\infty = 0$ on every sample). The harness therefore manufactures no deltas of its own, and the effects in Table~\ref{tab:crossfamily} are responses to the edits rather than to re-running the forward pass. This is now an asserted invariant in the audit script, not an observation.

\emph{A units caveat that applies to the $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ column only.} DeepThinkVLA un-normalizes actions by LIBERO quantiles, so its $\Delta_\infty$ is in physical units, whereas the ECoT decode of Section~\ref{app:sec:benchmark} stops at the normalized $[-1,1]$ range. The checkpoint's own $q_{99}-q_{01}$ is $[1.64, 1.67, 1.88, 0.25, 0.36, 0.56, 2.00]$ per DoF against a normalized width of $2.00$, so a fixed $\tau = 0.05$ is a \emph{stricter} test on DeepThinkVLA --- by $1.00$--$1.22\times$ on the translation and gripper dimensions that dominate an $L_\infty$ (the gripper channel's quantiles are exactly $\pm 1$, so that dimension is not rescaled at all), and by $3.6$--$8.1\times$ on the three rotation dimensions. Two consequences. First, the $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ column is \emph{not} comparable digit-for-digit across the horizontal rule in Table~\ref{tab:crossfamily}, which is one of the reasons this table is not merged into Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard}. Second, and more importantly, it does not touch the finding: floor, ceiling and $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ are all computed within a single run under a single threshold, so the threshold cancels in $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ and in the two-sided statistic, and the direction of the bias is to \emph{understate} DeepThinkVLA's $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ --- which if anything makes a negative $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ harder to obtain, not easier.

What this section does \emph{not} establish: \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} cannot be run on this architecture at all, since the CoT renderer emits no bounding boxes and the edit therefore yields a byte-identical trace ($n{=}0$, $100$ skipped). The numeric-perturbation floor that bounds decode brittleness on the ECoT family is consequently unavailable here, and that is a limit of this section rather than a robustness result. \emph{instr\_random\_sub} \emph{is} measured on all three checkpoints, and it does not come back in the metric's favour: the CoT-specificity ratio is $0.996$, $0.806$ and $0.814$, so none of the three clears its own out-of-CoT control (Table~\ref{tab:calibration}). \textbf{F7: P2 now covers two architecture families, and the finding that magnitude $\mathcal{F}$ is uninterpretable without its floor holds in both --- more strongly in the family that shares none of ECoT's design choices.}

\subsubsection{Ancillary: prompt-format ablation}

Figure~\ref{fig:prompt} shows that removing any portion of the CoT (task\_only, plan\_only, shuffled, empty) causes $\geq 95\%$ of samples to change action, confirming ECoT-bridge is strongly conditioned on the full nine-tag target. Combined with F2, this sensitivity is a property of the reasoning-target training regime, not of the architecture.

% ============================================================
\subsection{Discussion and limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}
% ============================================================

\paragraph{Threshold and metric sensitivity.} The Faithfulness Score threshold $\tau = 0.05$ was fixed \emph{a priori} as 5\% of the normalized action range. Because our per-sample $\Delta_\infty$ distributions are strongly bimodal (either $=0$, indicating the tokenizer produced an identical action, or $\gg 0.10$), Faithfulness Scores are stable under threshold perturbations. Figure~\ref{fig:threshold} plots mean faithful rate over 7 non-control families as a function of $\tau \in [0.01, 0.30]$ for 6 models: rankings are preserved across every threshold, and the qualitative gap between the no-CoT variant and the CoT-trained cluster is maintained.

\emph{We drew the weaker of the two available conclusions from that bimodality, and the stronger one is unflattering.} Over all $28{,}443$ scored records in the release, $46.2\%$ have $\Delta_\infty$ \emph{exactly} zero and $44.5\%$ exceed $0.10$; of the records that move at all, only $9.8\%$ land below $\tau$. If almost no mass lies between $0$ and the threshold, then $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ is not measuring how far the action moved --- it is close to counting how often the decode failed to collide. We measured that directly. Across the $324$ (run, family) cells with $n \geq 20$, $\mathcal{F}$ at $\tau{=}0.05$ tracks $1 - P(\Delta_\infty = 0)$ at $r = 0.963$, $R^2 = 0.926$, with $80$ cells identical to the last digit and a global difference of $0.485$ against $0.538$. \textbf{Threshold-insensitivity is therefore a consequence of the metric being nearly a collision counter, not evidence that it is robust}, and Figure~\ref{fig:threshold} should be read as showing the former. This does not invalidate any comparison in the paper --- a collision rate is a well-defined and self-consistent quantity, and every $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$ we report is computed the same way --- but it does change what the quantity is called, and it is the mechanism behind Section~\ref{sec:paraphrase_null}: a score whose dynamic range is dominated by argmax collisions has no particular reason to separate meaning-changing edits from meaning-preserving ones, and it does not. We release the per-cell decomposition at \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}collision\_\allowbreak{}decomposition/\allowbreak{}} and report $P(\Delta_\infty = 0)$ as a first-class column in Table~\ref{tab:collision} so that a reader can see the two quantities side by side rather than taking the correlation on our word.

\begin{figure*}[t]

    \includegraphics[width=0.65\textwidth]{fig11_threshold_sensitivity.pdf}
    \caption{\textbf{Faithfulness Score threshold sensitivity.} Mean \emph{magnitude} faithful rate over 7 non-control families vs $\tau \in [0.01, 0.30]$ (log scale). Magnitude-score rankings are preserved across the full range and the no-CoT vs CoT-trained gap remains $\geq 2\times$ at every $\tau$, so our conclusions are not artifacts of $\tau{=}0.05$. This is robustness of the magnitude score to $\tau$ only; it does not address the direction-blindness of Section~\ref{app:sec:directional}, which no choice of $\tau$ can fix.}
    \label{fig:threshold}
\end{figure*}
