\paragraph{What is missing.} We list every gap we are aware of, including the ones that weaken the paper.

\emph{(i) Construct validity fails on 11 of the 12 calibration entries, in both architecture families, and the one exception is the negative control.} The calibration nulls have now been run on every model in the benchmark (Table~\ref{tab:calibration}), which replaces the submission's two calibrated rows with twelve --- eleven distinct checkpoints across two architecture families --- and lets this item be stated as a rate rather than an anecdote. On $\mathbf{11}$ of $\mathbf{12}$ entries $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ sits \emph{below} that model's own paraphrase floor ($\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ from $-0.179$ to $+0.014$), and the two-sided statistic is negative on $\mathbf{9}$ of the $10$ entries where it is defined --- on \emph{all eight} non-degenerate full-CoT variants, whose floors ($0.45$--$0.82$) are nowhere near their ceilings, and six of those eight are ours while two are DeepThinkVLA. \textbf{So a meaning-preserving synonym swap moves the action more reliably than a semantic edit does, on every full-CoT model we have measured, in both architecture families}, and $\mathcal{F}$ is not licensed as a reading of CoT$\to$action semantic causal flow on any of them. The single positive two-sided score in the paper is the independent retraining of the no-CoT variant ($+0.127$) --- the model trained on an action-only target, which is exactly where a working floor-corrected statistic \emph{should} return approximately its own floor, so we report it as the protocol's one clean model-level positive control rather than as a model that passes. Two encouraging signals survive at $n{=}12$: the numeric meaning-preserving perturbation \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} scores only $0.047$--$0.087$ on the eight trained ECoT variants (against $0.460$ on the saturated ECoT-bridge), so $\mathcal{F}$ is not pure brittleness --- it ignores a meaning-preserving numeric change more than $91\%$ of the time; and exactly $2$ of the $12$ calibrations are degenerate, and they are the two \emph{saturated} public checkpoints, one per architecture family (ECoT-bridge at a dynamic range of $0.010$ and DeepThinkVLA-base at $0.020$, against $0.067$--$0.337$ on the other ten, up to $34\times$ wider), with no full-CoT trained variant degenerate in either family --- which \textbf{localizes the collapse to the saturated regime rather than to the protocol or to one CoT format} on ten contrasting models across two architectures instead of eight within one. \emph{(ii) The calibration set is now complete: all three nulls on all 11 models, in both architecture families, with one family inapplicable-by-construction rather than missing.} The seven ``ours'' leaderboard rows, ECoT-bridge, the no-CoT retraining, and the three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints all have full 13-family runs, so $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$, the two-sided statistic and the CoT-specificity ratio are defined on \emph{every} model in the benchmark --- up from five, two and two respectively at submission, and up from nine, nine and nine at the previous revision, where the second architecture family was the open gap this item named. The cross-family comparison of the out-of-CoT check is therefore no longer open, and its answer is adverse to the metric: the specificity ratio is below $1$ on all three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints ($0.996$, $0.806$, $0.814$), so every entry that clears the control is an ECoT variant trained by us. One cell is genuinely absent: \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} on the DeepThinkVLA rows, and \emph{absent is the correct outcome} rather than a gap in our runs --- that family perturbs bounding-box coordinates and DeepThinkVLA's CoT renderer emits none, so the edit produces a byte-identical trace. The harness records $n{=}0$ with all $100$ samples skipped. This item previously said the family was ``still missing'' on those checkpoints, which understated the problem: our own committed artifacts had it at $n{=}100$, $\mathcal{F}=0.000$, with every $\Delta$ identically zero --- a vacuous identity edit reported as perfect robustness to a meaning-preserving perturbation, and numerically indistinguishable from \emph{selfsplice\_control}. The guard that now refuses to score an unrendered edit is what turned that into a stated applicability fact, and it also moved \emph{location\_swap} on those three checkpoints from $N{=}70$ to $N{=}58$; the superseded runs are retained under \texttt{results\_v2/superseded/}. The consequence for F2 is no longer a missing measurement but a measured result that cuts two ways, and Section~\ref{sec:f2_calib} states both: the two-sided recomputation of the F2 table is now possible and is \emph{negative on all seven} rows, so the one-sided ordering must not be read as floor-corrected; but the out-of-CoT contrast F2 needed does hold in \emph{direction} on 5 of the 6 CoT-trained variants and fails, as required, on no-CoT --- so \textbf{F2 does not dissolve}, it narrows to an absolute-effect-size claim whose margin over the out-of-CoT control survives training-run variance on \emph{none} of those 6. \emph{(iii) Direction-blindness changes the ordering, which is why we publish no ranking.} The magnitude ordering inverts under direction-aware scoring (Section~\ref{app:sec:directional}). Rather than pick one, Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} bolds nothing and Section~\ref{sec:results} states that no ranking is licensed by it; we recommend $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ for any claim about semantic steerability. \emph{(iv) P3 is re-run in-domain and its result is negative.} The submitted AUROCs were withdrawn, not merely caveated, for the cross-domain-plus-mixed-units protocol error documented in Section~\ref{sec:analysis}. The corrected run (Section~\ref{sec:p3_indomain}) scores the same checkpoint on its own training corpus in robot units, and finds $\alpha(m,\text{cot})$ at $0.596$ with a 95\% CI spanning chance: on the one model we can run in-domain, CoT attention does not predict per-sample action error. Only $\alpha(m,\text{instruction})$ excludes chance ($0.362$, CI $[0.284, 0.469]$), in the direction that inattention to the command predicts error, and that direction was read off the same data rather than predicted in advance. Three further limits: $N{=}153$ rather than the requested $200$, because that is what the Bridge~V2 loader yielded; the CoT is self-generated, since Bridge carries no ground-truth reasoning, so the probe cannot separate ``attention does not predict error'' from ``attention over a self-generated trace does not predict error''; and it is one model, so P3 supports no cross-model comparison at all. We do not generalize the negative result beyond this checkpoint. \emph{(v) Rollout-level faithfulness is still absent from the leaderboard, and the decoder gate failed four times before it passed.} The leaderboard uses first-step observations, and that is a design choice this item does not retract; what it does retract is a hedge four earlier versions of it carried. Our first diagnostic rollout returned Task SR $=0/20$ from a scoring bug (success read from \texttt{info["success"]}, a key LIBERO never sets). A second attempt returned nonzero-but-wrong numbers for a different reason: LIBERO's \texttt{.pruned\_init} files are \texttt{torch.save} archives, our loader read them with \texttt{np.load}, and every episode therefore fell back to a random \texttt{env.reset()} rather than the suite's canonical evaluation initial state. Both runs exited $0$ and wrote a well-formed report, which is the defect worth naming: a broken evaluation that is indistinguishable from a real one. The loader now raises instead of falling back, a unit test asserts that on garbage input, and every rollout report records how many episodes used canonical init states, so this particular failure cannot recur silently. A third attempt then had verified canonical initial states on $50/50$ episodes and still scored $0/50$ on two suites --- Table~\ref{tab:gate}, best interpretable cell $5/50 = 0.10$ on \emph{libero\_goal} against a published $0.794$, with \emph{libero\_10} excluded for a step budget below upstream's --- which is what established that a third, independent cause remained after the two we had fixed. A source-level diff against \texttt{openvla/openvla} produced two candidates for it, an unapplied $g \mapsto -\operatorname{sign}(2g-1)$ gripper convention and a skipped JPEG-plus-lanczos3 frame preprocessing step, and both were measured rather than assumed and both came back null: the gripper factor alone leaves SR at $0/10$ under all four conventions we can construct for it, and the $2{\times}2$ factorial over gripper and image preprocessing scores $0/10$ in every cell including the one that applies both corrections (Section~\ref{sec:analysis}). \textbf{The third cause was the action decode itself} --- the one component validated only by our own offline audit rather than against upstream's code path, and the one each of those three nulls had unknowingly been testing \emph{on top of}. Calling the checkpoint's own \texttt{predict\_action} in place of our masked-argmax loop, with the gripper convention applied on top of it, brings Task SR to $0.74$, $0.90$, $0.74$ and $0.46$ on \emph{libero\_spatial}, \emph{libero\_object}, \emph{libero\_goal} and \emph{libero\_10} at upstream's own per-suite step budgets --- $0.853$ to $1.022$ of published --- while the in-run anchor arms, which keep the corrected decoder and drop only the gripper convention, score $0.00$, $0.00$, $0.12$ and $0.00$, so both corrections are necessary and neither alone suffices on any suite. \emph{libero\_10}, the one suite Table~\ref{tab:gate} had to exclude as uninterpretable, is now in the gate at upstream's own $520$-step budget and scores $23/50$. \textbf{The gate passes on all four suites} (Table~\ref{tab:gate_pass}), which is every suite upstream publishes a LIBERO checkpoint for, so this is the whole gate rather than three quarters of one. Two limits on what that buys, because the temptation is to over-read it. It licenses the statement that the checkpoint is competent at the task inside our harness, which is what retires the harness as a candidate explanation elsewhere in this paper. It does \emph{not} make any number here rollout-conditioned, and it does not by itself establish that our deltas are correctly scaled. It is worth being precise about what the earlier failed gate did and did not contaminate, because our own phrasing had this backwards. The edit protocol's action decode (\texttt{experiments/\allowbreak{}cotfaith\_\allowbreak{}edit.py}) maps action token ids to bin indices and de-quantizes to the normalized $[-1,1]$ range; it never consults \texttt{norm\_stats}, and \texttt{unnorm\_key} does not appear anywhere in that code path. The frame mismatch that withdrew P3 --- Bridge de-normalization statistics applied to LIBERO episodes (Section~\ref{sec:analysis}) --- is therefore \emph{structurally incapable} of altering any $\Delta_\infty$ reported here, and the offline audit's adverse numbers ($L_1$ $13\times$ worse than predicting the dataset mean, flat correlation $-0.69$) are evidence about that broken cross-domain configuration, not about the policy or about the edit cells. What the passing rollout gate establishes is that the policy is competent at the task, \emph{not} that our deltas are correctly scaled; those are different claims and we now have the first without inheriting the second, so we still claim only what the construction gives us: every $\mathcal{F}$ here is a first-step paired-intervention quantity in normalized action units. The P2 decode path itself is no longer taken on trust either: it is compared against the checkpoint's own \texttt{predict\_action} and selects byte-identical tokens on $66/66$ prompts with $0/54$ flags moved (Section~\ref{sec:analysis}), which bounds --- on one checkpoint, at that $N$ --- the exposure of the published $\mathcal{F}$ to the defect that the rollout decoder turned out to have. One structural obstacle to the rollout-level protocol is now measured rather than suspected, and it changed which checkpoint the protocol can run on: \texttt{ecot-openvla-7b-bridge} ships \texttt{norm\_stats} for \texttt{bridge\_orig} only, so on LIBERO its actions cannot be de-quantized to world scale and Task SR is pinned at $0$ in every arm including the unedited control, for a reason with nothing to do with the CoT (Section~\ref{sec:analysis}; probe released with its compute-platform task id). The paired rollout is therefore run on our own \mbox{r=32} LIBERO fine-tune, whose native action scale is the identity. \textbf{That run has now completed in-suite, and it returns a bound rather than a measurement, for a reason we can name.} At $40$ episodes per arm on \emph{libero\_90} at upstream's own step budget, the clean-CoT arm scores Task SR $=0/40$ (Wilson $95\%$ $[0.000, 0.088]$) having generated $640$ CoTs, and the no-CoT arm scores $0/40$ over the same episodes (Wilson $95\%$ $[0.000, 0.088]$) having generated none. \textbf{The two arms are identical, so the zero is not attributable to the CoT}: an edit-induced $\Delta$SR is undefined when the unedited control never succeeds, and our harness defines it as $0$ by construction in that state rather than reporting a difference. \textbf{Four pairing defects in this harness, each found only because we checked the previous fix instead of declaring it fixed --- the first two by re-rendering, the third and fourth by a probe that takes the policy out of the loop --- and reported here because no scalar in any of those runs could have shown them.} ``Over the same episodes'' is exact for the robot and for every free object and \emph{inexact} for the furniture. \texttt{set\_init\_state} restores the flattened MuJoCo state --- \texttt{qpos}/\texttt{qvel} --- so it restores the arm and everything resting on the table; a fixture welded to the world body has no joint, its pose lives in the model rather than in \texttt{qpos}, and robosuite's placement sampler draws it when the environment is \emph{constructed}. These runs built one environment per arm, so each arm drew its own furniture placement and \texttt{set\_init\_state} could not undo it. We measured it on the one run of this harness that renders pixels, a frame-capture run over the same suite and checkpoint (compute-platform \texttt{h8xzmqnhgg}): at step $0$, before either arm has acted, the two arms differ over $10.4\%$ of the frame and are \textbf{bit-identical} --- $0.0000$ mean absolute pixel --- everywhere outside the bounding box of that difference. Inside the box the mean is $8.8411$, and translating the box by $3$ pixels cuts the residual to $2.7762$, which is the signature of one rigid object placed differently rather than of a policy that acted differently. Neither region is chosen by us: the box is wherever the difference is, and the $0.0000$ is its complement. \textbf{No number in this paper changes, for any of the four.} Task SR is $0/40$ in both arms, so $\Delta$SR was already undefined, and two failures are not made more or less identical by moving a drawer $3$ pixels. What the disclosure retracts is the \emph{strength} of ``the same episodes'', which held for exactly the state \texttt{set\_init\_state} restores and not for the scene around it. The first fix was to build one environment per \emph{episode} and separate the arms with \texttt{set\_init\_state} alone, with no \texttt{reset()} between them --- \texttt{reset()} is what re-runs the placement sampler --- and additionally to seed that sampler per (task, episode), so the pairing no longer rests on an assumption about which RNG places fixtures. Re-rendering under that fix showed that it had worked and that it was not sufficient. \textbf{The second defect: the arms still differed at step $0$, and this time over the robot} (compute-platform \texttt{xyiztdu4n6}). The furniture was now bit-identical --- $0.0000$ outside the differing box again, and the box had moved off the cabinet to rows $0$--$134$ --- but inside it the mean was $31.7356$ and \emph{no} translation reduced it: the best shift was $(0,0)$, leaving the residual exactly where it started. A pose that no shift aligns is a differently posed robot rather than a differently placed object, so this is a second defect and not an incomplete fix of the first. Its cause is the ten no-op settling steps that let objects come to rest after \texttt{set\_init\_state} writes them into place. Each arm ran its own, and \texttt{set\_init\_state} restores \texttt{qpos}/\texttt{qvel} and nothing else, so the arm that ran second entered its settle carrying the previous arm's operational-space controller goal and MuJoCo's warm-start accelerations --- neither of which is in the flattened state --- and ten steps of contact dynamics amplified that into a visibly different arm pose before the first frame was written. Settling is a property of the scene and not of any arm, so the harness now runs it once per episode, snapshots the result, and rewinds every arm to that snapshot with both carry-over channels cleared; this makes the first frame identical \emph{by construction}, since the render is a function of the model and \texttt{qpos}, rather than by trusting ten steps of dynamics to be reproducible --- an inference the fourth defect below \emph{falsifies}, and we leave it stated in the form we believed it because it is the assumption that hid the next defect for two runs. \textbf{The third defect: an identical first frame cannot see the confound that matters most.} Step-$0$ identity is necessary and not sufficient. The channels \texttt{set\_init\_state} does not restore act from step $1$ onward --- exactly where the arms are \emph{supposed} to differ --- so a confound there is invisible in the pixels and in every scalar of the report. We therefore removed the policy: settle once, rewind twice, and replay one fixed scripted action sequence both times (\texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}probe\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}rewind\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}pairing.py}, compute-platform \texttt{gzv4nuhtfe}). Two identical prompts must give identical trajectories, and they did not. Both known channels \emph{were} reset --- the artifact records \texttt{controller:\ 1}, \texttt{warmstart:\ true}, so the paragraph above is not overstating the fix --- and yet the two replays differed by $0.1876$ in \texttt{qpos} and by $198$ pixel levels, with the maximum over all steps \emph{equal} to the first-step difference and not growing after it: a stale offset rather than accumulating drift. The offset is robosuite's gripper. Its \texttt{current\_action} is a rate-limited accumulator, advanced by a fixed increment per control step, and it lives in neither the model nor \texttt{qpos}, so \texttt{set\_init\_state} does not restore it and the controller reset --- which is about the arm --- does not touch it; an arm running second therefore began with the previous arm's gripper part-way through a close. The settle now snapshots it and every rewind restores that snapshot, restoring rather than zeroing, because zeroing would put the scene at a fresh-reset value instead of where the settle actually left it. \textbf{The fourth defect: identical state, different frame.} Rewinding all three channels made the two replays identical in \texttt{qpos} and did \emph{not} make them identical in pixels (compute-platform \texttt{e268dqs2t8}). Over $40$ steps of the same scripted sequence the arms agree to $0.0$ in \texttt{qpos} at \emph{every} step and disagree in the render at every step, by up to $160$ levels, with $0.0000$ mean absolute pixel outside the differing box and \emph{no} translation aligning the two frames at any step ($0/40$ steps have an exact shifted match, against a rigid $3$-pixel offset for defect~1). The mechanism is a phase and not a pose. robosuite calls \texttt{\_update\_observables()} \emph{inside} the physics substep loop and resamples an observable when its own \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}since\_\allowbreak{}last\_\allowbreak{}sample} reaches the sampling interval, so which substep the returned camera frame is taken from is decided by a per-observable clock --- and that clock is in neither the model nor \texttt{qpos}. At rewind the two arms' clocks differed by $1.1 \times 10^{-15}$ ($0.004000000000000278$ against $0.004000000000001388$, carried by $31$ of the $206$ observable fields), which is enough to put the comparison on opposite sides of the interval boundary and hand one arm a frame from a different substep. \textbf{A difference in the last representable digit of a timer became a $116$-level difference in the image the policy is shown}, and this is the defect this paper is least entitled to have missed: the state was bit-identical, so every check we had ran green.

All three rows are the same pixels at $t{=}0$ --- max mean $|\Delta\text{pixel}| = 0.0$ --- which is what the four pairing fixes above bought, and which the generator verifies before it draws rather than after. \textbf{(b)} the top-down gripper path. The arm reading its \emph{own} reasoning is the one that barely travels: its whole path fits in a $21.8$\,cm box, while both other arms cross the workspace. \textbf{(c)} per-step distance from the clean-CoT arm, which peaks at $139.7$\,cm for the flipped arm and $128.8$\,cm for the no-CoT arm. \textbf{None of this is a faithfulness measurement.} All three arms score $0$, so no $\Delta$SR is defined (item~(v)), and one episode of one task supports no ranking of anything. Between-column change \emph{within} an arm runs $0.04$--$7.7$ absolute pixel levels (means $2.4$--$3.8$), so two near-identical adjacent cells are a policy that has stalled and not a repeated frame. \textbf{Which is why the probe now measures the state-to-pixel implication instead of arguing it.} The fix adds the sampling phase to the rewind --- the clock and the cached observable values, alongside the controller goal, the warm-start accelerations and the gripper accumulator --- and after it all $206$ observable fields agree between arms ($0$ differing, against $31$ before) and all $38$ render inputs we can enumerate agree. \textbf{The result is the first run of this harness in which the arms are bit-identical: max absolute pixel difference $0.0$ over all $40$ steps, on both arm pairs} (compute-platform \texttt{vu6yavsp4a}; channels restored \texttt{controller:\ 1}, \texttt{warmstart:\ true}, \texttt{gripper:\ 1}, \texttt{clock:\ 3}, \texttt{observables:\ 29}). The probe also writes down the implication that defect~4 falsified, as a standing fact rather than an assumption: with the same state written into the environment and re-rendered, \texttt{state\_\allowbreak{}determines\_\allowbreak{}frame} is \texttt{false} at $116$ levels. So a rendered frame is not a function of \texttt{qpos} in this simulator, and no future fix of ours may be validated on state alone. \textbf{No published number moves, for the same reason as the first three}: both in-suite rollout runs predate this fix, and Task SR is $0$ in every arm of both, so $\Delta$SR was already undefined and already recorded as \texttt{precondition\_\allowbreak{}met:\ false}; the two protocol-level quantities the second run contributes ($381$ skipped edits, a $10.2\%$ post-edit parse-failure rate) are properties of the CoT text and its parser, which the render phase does not enter. What the fix buys is that the first rollout comparison anyone runs on this harness will be paired at the pixel level, which none of the ones reported here were. The probe now gates on all five channels, so one that a future robosuite renames is reported instead of silently skipped. Three layers then refuse to proceed if any two arms differ at step $0$: the rollout script, while the GPU is still allocated; the figure generator, rather than drawing rows whose differences a reader would attribute to the edit; and an offline unit test, run against the real defective frames. Figure~\ref{fig:filmstrip} is the first strip to pass all three, drawn from a fifth capture run at per-step CoT: it is the only exhibit in this paper in which a CoT edit and the motion it produced appear in the same picture, and it is included \emph{because} the scalars for that run are all $0$ --- two arms that both score $0/1$ are indistinguishable in the record even when one of them has left the table. We report it at this length because it is the class of defect this paper is about: every scalar in that report was correct, and only the pixels showed it. All three diagnostics are released as \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}v2/\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}canonical\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}runs/\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}rollout\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}arm\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}pairing\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}defect/\allowbreak{}} together with \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}diagnose\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}arm\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{\allowbreak{}}pairing.py} and the probe above, which produce them. The competence reason is measured and is the same one that keeps P3 withdrawn on these weights: the frame check in \texttt{auroc\_\allowbreak{}indomain\_\allowbreak{}ours\_\allowbreak{}null/\allowbreak{}} finds this checkpoint's open-loop single-step L$_1$ ($0.0486$) \emph{worse} than predicting the per-dimension dataset mean ($0.0457$, ratio $1.063$) in every frame it ships, so it fails criterion (iii) of our own gate at Section~\ref{sec:analysis}. \textbf{We therefore state plainly that the missing rollout evidence is a checkpoint-competence problem and not a compute or suite-availability problem}, which is how four earlier versions of this item framed it. A rollout-level faithfulness measurement needs a policy whose clean success rate is well clear of zero; the tractable path is a public checkpoint with documented nonzero SR rather than our own, and we do not have that result. No rollout-conditioned number appears anywhere in this paper. \textbf{A second in-suite run has since added the edited arm the first stopped short of} (compute-platform \texttt{nskmsunnpb}, released under \texttt{rollout\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}insuite\_\allowbreak{}flip/\allowbreak{}}): under the same wall-clock budget a third arm costs episodes, so it is $10/10/9$ rather than $40/40$, and \emph{direction\_flip} returns $0/9$ against the same $0/10$ controls. \textbf{An edited arm does not make the comparison defined}: $0$ against a control that never succeeds is $0$ because both terms are, and the harness again records \texttt{precondition\_\allowbreak{}met: false} with no $\Delta$SR. What the run does establish is that the edit protocol runs closed-loop end to end --- generate, parse, edit, re-inject, decode, refreshed every $25$ steps --- and it produces two numbers the first-step protocol cannot. $381$ edits were \emph{skipped} mid-rollout because the CoT at that step carried no direction word to reverse, which bounds how often \emph{direction\_flip} is even applicable along a trajectory as against the first steps every published number is measured on; and editing the CoT raises the \emph{next} generation's parse-failure rate to $10.2\%$ from the clean arm's $0.2\%$. We report both as properties of the protocol, not as results about faithfulness, since with SR pinned at $0$ neither can be connected to behaviour.\emph{(vi) Attention: the layer set is load-bearing, and the error bars now come from a retraining replicate on every row.} A $5$-layer-set $\times$ $3$-seed sweep ($15$ runs, $N{=}100$ each) shows $\alpha(\text{cot})$ leads in exactly $1$ of the $4$ four-layer blocks probed --- layers $0$--$3$, the block we reported --- and that $\alpha(\text{cot})$ swings $18.7$\,pp across depth ($0.157$ at layers $8$--$11$ to $0.344$ at $0$--$3$, non-monotone) against a worst-case sampling $\sigma$ of $0.26$\,pp, a ratio of $72\times$. So every attention claim here is an early-layer claim, the ordering our layer set produces is the one that does \emph{not} generalize, and no bucket ordering should be reported without its layer set. Separately, sampling noise is now measured at $\sigma \leq 0.094$\,pp at the reported layer set and $\leq 0.26$\,pp across all five (3 seeds, $N{=}100$ each), but the relevant floor is same-config training-run variation, and \textbf{we now have a pair for every trained row rather than two}: $|\Delta\alpha(\text{cot})|$ of $0.12$, $0.14$, $0.56$, $0.56$, $0.73$, $1.45$ and $1.95$\,pp against a $2.30$\,pp within-ECoT spread --- a ratio of $1.2\times$, \emph{tighter} than the $1.6\times$ two pairs suggested, because the widest retraining gap in the benchmark turned out to belong to a configuration that had no replicate when this item was written. So no within-ECoT ordering is supported, and that now rests on a seven-point distribution rather than a magnitude. What remains future work is narrower: one replicate per configuration gives each pair's own difference a single degree of freedom, so we bound the noise without estimating a per-model variance. \emph{(vii) Sample sizes vary by family, but no longer by row.} $10$ of the $13$ families report $N{=}100$ on every ``ours'' row; \emph{subject\_swap}, \emph{adversarial\_plausible} and \emph{selfsplice\_control} report $N{=}69$ (skipped when the target object is not visible in the frame), and \emph{location\_swap} reports $N{=}74$. The corresponding ECoT-bridge values are $100$, $60$ and $70$. The submitted version of this table had \emph{location\_swap} at $N{=}12$ on the seven ``ours'' rows, because those runs predated the C5 annotation fix that expanded the location list; every row is now post-fix, so \textbf{the $N{=}12$ cells are gone and per-family $N$ is uniform across rows} --- which is what makes the column-wise comparisons in Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} well-posed at all. All $8 \times 11$ cells of Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} carry a real 3-seed point estimate and there are no unmeasured entries left in it, including the \emph{para} column, per (ii). The residual $N$ asymmetry between the ``ours'' rows ($69$/$74$) and ECoT-bridge ($60$/$70$) is a difference in which frames the visibility gate admits, not in protocol, and it is why we compare each model only against its own floor and ceiling. \emph{(viii) Seeds are now on every row, and the error bar that matters is still not the seed.} All 8 rows of Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} are 3-sampling-seed means with Wilson 95\% CIs on pooled counts (half-widths $\leq 0.067$), replacing the submission's single-run point estimates on seven of them. \textbf{This does not fix the problem it might appear to fix.} Sampling seeds hold the checkpoint fixed, so they bound the \emph{sample} draw, and we now have seven measurements showing that is the smaller term. \textbf{All seven trained configurations were trained a second time} at a byte-identical recipe and the same seed, and every replicate was scored at the same evaluation seed on the same $100$ samples with byte-identical interventions (on the $r{=}32$ pair: $791$ common scored records, all $791$ with identical \texttt{edit\_meta}) --- and each pair is two different models: on $r{=}32$ the \emph{unedited} action differs on $66$ of the $100$ samples, by up to $1.99$ per dimension. Over the nine families whose $N$ matches across a pair, $\mathcal{F}$ moves by a mean of $0.024$--$0.079$ and a maximum of $\mathbf{0.260}$ (\emph{verb\_swap} $0.700 \rightarrow 0.960$ on $r{=}8$; the per-pair maxima are $0.060$, $0.067$, $0.083$, $0.130$, $0.170$, $0.180$, $0.260$), and the summary statistic $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ itself moves $0.006$--$0.092$. The worst family is \emph{verb\_swap} on three of the seven pairs, so this is not one anomalous cell. The $0.260$ is ${\sim}3.9\times$ the widest Wilson half-width in the table and larger than most of the between-model differences a reader would want to read off it. This is the same conclusion the attention sweep reached ($0.12$--$1.95$\,pp of training-run noise against $\leq 0.094$\,pp of sampling noise) arriving on the edit metric at ${\sim}10\times$ the magnitude. Three consequences we state rather than absorb: the Wilson intervals in Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} are \emph{not} the right error bars for comparing two variants trained by us; single-family differences below ${\sim}0.26$ on those rows should not be read as model differences at all; and the $0.092$ worst-case movement in $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ is the yardstick against which every CoT-specificity margin in Section~\ref{sec:f2_calib} is judged, which is what reduces the F2 out-of-CoT result from six variants to \emph{none} --- under the two-pair floor this item previously reported, two of the six appeared to survive it. The controls behave as they should across all seven retrainings --- \emph{selfsplice\_control} is exactly $0.000$ in all $14$ runs --- so this is variance in the measured quantity, not in the harness; the ceiling control \emph{cross\_task\_swap} is not exempt from it, moving $0.000$--$0.130$. \textbf{The item this used to defer is now closed}: retraining replicates exist for all seven variants, as item (vi) also records for attention, and what remains is that one replicate per configuration bounds the noise without estimating a per-model variance. Artifacts \texttt{ours\_\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}lora-r8,\allowbreak{}lora-r16,\allowbreak{}lora-r32,\allowbreak{}lora-r64,\allowbreak{}data-50A,\allowbreak{}data-50B\}\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}13family\_\allowbreak{}RETRAIN.json}, \texttt{ours\_\allowbreak{}no-cot\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}13family\_\allowbreak{}calibration.json}, their \texttt{\_rvis\_RETRAIN.json} counterparts, the run-A files they pair with, and \texttt{retrain2\_\allowbreak{}provenance.json}, which records each replicate's training arguments and compute-platform task id. \emph{(ix) Coverage.} OpenVLA-OFT failed to load cleanly in our environment (Python 3.10, torch 2.4.1, transformers 4.40.1 --- the pins \texttt{bolt/setup-openvla.sh} actually installs; an earlier version of this sentence cited torch 2.2.0, an environment this release no longer runs). Six rounds of that probe were inconclusive for a reason worth stating, because it is the failure mode this item was in danger of committing: every round held torch at ours so the $2\times2$ of \{baseline, upgraded\}~$\times$~\{with, without \texttt{prismatic}\} would stay comparable, which meant the one torch never exercised was the \texttt{torch==2.2.0} that \texttt{openvla-oft} itself declares. A seventh round adds a fifth cell in an isolated virtualenv at that declared pin, deliberately outside the cross-stage torch check (compute-platform \texttt{d3xygfkrke}; the cell reports \texttt{torch 2.2.0+cu121} against the grid's \texttt{2.4.1+cu118}, so it is a distinct environment rather than a relabelled repeat). All five \texttt{moojink/\allowbreak{}openvla-7b-oft-*} repos still fail, and they fail at weight loading rather than at import --- \texttt{TypeError: cumsum() received an invalid combination of arguments - got (bool,\allowbreak{} dim=int)} --- in all $5$ stages, \texttt{any\_loaded=False} throughout. \textbf{The OFT family is therefore excluded for a measured reason, at the environment its own authors specify, not for an untested one.} Separately, the DeepThinkVLA family is attention-only in this version --- the edit protocol produced no scored pairs on it because we ported OpenVLA's action-decode conventions wholesale to a checkpoint initialized from \texttt{pi0fast\_base}, and \emph{all six} of them are wrong for it: the action ids are $2{,}048$ slots inside PaliGemma's base vocabulary ($254976$--$257023$) rather than the top $256$; the bin index is reversed within that window; the $70$ action positions ($10$ chunk steps $\times$ $7$ DoF) are decoded in one forward pass under a hybrid causal/bidirectional mask rather than by \texttt{generate()}; the output is a $(10,7)$ chunk rather than a single $7$-vector; and LIBERO actions are quantile-normalized ($q_{01}/q_{99}$), not min--max. No generated token ever fell in the assumed range. The fix does not guess among candidates: we vendor upstream's own MIT-licensed model class (\texttt{anonrepo/\allowbreak{}vendor/\allowbreak{}deepthinkvla/\allowbreak{}}, with commit sha, byte sha256, and an exhaustive edit list), \emph{assert} all six conventions against the checkpoint's \texttt{config.json} at load time, and \emph{raise} rather than write an empty report. Those corrected runs are now complete and reported in Section~\ref{sec:cross_family}: all three checkpoints decode $100/100$ with zero failures across all $12$ applicable families, so \textbf{P2 now covers two architecture families}, and both of the adverse findings replicate on the second one. The three checkpoints have since also been run on the full 13-family calibration set, which closes the coverage gap earlier versions of this item named: \emph{instr\_random\_sub} is measured on all three, so the out-of-CoT specificity check is defined on all $11$ models rather than $9$, and \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} is inapplicable to this architecture by construction rather than unrun (item (ii)). \textbf{The gate is a second, separate coverage claim, and \emph{libero\_90} cannot be part of it.} Upstream publishes exactly four LIBERO checkpoints (\emph{spatial}, \emph{object}, \emph{goal}, \emph{libero\_10}) and no \emph{libero\_90} checkpoint, and therefore no published success rate to gate against; a \emph{libero\_90} row would have no reference value and no fine-tuned policy, so the four-suite gate is the complete gate rather than a subset of a five-suite one. We state that rather than leave the suite listed as future work. OpenVLA-OFT remains unloadable in our environment. \emph{(x) One edit family's name overstates what it does, and we found that by measuring our own generators rather than by being told.} The families are defined by claims about their own semantics, and until this revision those claims were asserted from generator source and never checked --- the same evidential status as the caveats this revision has been replacing with measurements, and a more consequential one, since $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ is a floor-corrected statistic only if its floor family is genuinely meaning-preserving. A blind LLM judge, itself gated on an identity control ($1.000$), a pooled negative control ($0.175$) and an order-agreement check ($0.824$), now reads $437$ edit pairs (Section~\ref{sec:judge_edits}). The load-bearing premises survive: \emph{paraphrase\_null} preserves meaning at $0.975$ and \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} at $1.000$, so the paraphrase floor and the numeric-floor argument are validated rather than assumed. One premise does not: \emph{adversarial\_plausible} changes the referent as designed ($0.958$) but is judged plausible on only $\mathbf{0.125}$ of its pairs, against a taxonomy entry that promised ``visually plausible but wrong''. The description is corrected in Section~\ref{sec:taxonomy}; the numbers are unchanged, because $\mathcal{F}$ does not depend on what the edit is called, and no claim in this paper rested on that family's plausibility --- but a benchmark whose taxonomy oversells one family would have been believed on the others too, which is why the check is now released as an artifact rather than described. Two by-products are limits in their own right. \emph{syntactic\_scramble}, listed in Tier~0 as a structural edit, preserves meaning at $1.000$ and is really a third meaning-preserving family. And \emph{verb\_swap} changes meaning on only $0.575$ of pairs, which we take to be the same fact as its being the worst same-config retraining cell in item~(viii): a generator that half the time produces no semantic change will produce an unstable $\mathcal{F}$. What is \emph{not} established is per-record correspondence --- the released records store actions only, so the judge validates the generators over the same corpus and the same demo files, not the exact scored pairs --- and it is one judge model at $n{=}40$ per family with a measured $17.6\%$ order-flip rate.

\paragraph{Implications for interpretability claims.} F1--F3 (plus the O4 observation and F5) together imply that ``attention on CoT is high'' does \emph{not} entail ``CoT drives the action'' --- and F6 adds that ``editing the CoT moves the action'' does not entail ``the CoT's meaning drives the action'' either. Any downstream system that reads or edits the CoT to steer VLA behavior must verify, on its own deployment distribution, both that $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ exceeds that model's paraphrase floor and that the induced action change points the intended way. The $N{=}100$ cross-corpus sweep (F5) shows the attention pipeline transfers to Bridge~V2, Fractal, and BC-Z; direction-aware causal effect does not transfer the same way and must be re-validated per corpus.

\paragraph{Public release, datasheet, and license.} The full artifact accompanies this submission as supplementary material: the 13 edit-family generators, \textbf{52{,}338} per-sample edit records of which $45{,}989$ carry a scored delta and $45{,}551$ of those carry the full action pair (original action, edited action, per-dimension delta, and the edit metadata that regenerates the edited CoT deterministically from the source trace and the released generator --- the records carry \texttt{edit\_meta}, \texttt{instruction} and \texttt{file\_base}, not the edited text itself; an earlier version of this sentence claimed the verbatim edited CoT was included and it is not, on any record; the remaining $6{,}349$ are recorded as skipped, with the reason, rather than dropped), \textbf{3{,}620} per-observation attention records with segment boundaries and token counts, the $200$ records behind the withdrawn P3 probe and the $153$ behind its in-domain re-run, the decoder audit, the five-stage OpenVLA-OFT load probe and the DeepThinkVLA decode-equivalence audit, and the derivation and audit scripts --- $52.7$\,MB of JSON in total, requiring no network access to re-derive any number in this paper. The record count is $3.2\times$ the submitted release: the growth is the 3-sampling-seed re-runs of all seven ``ours'' rows at 13 families each, which replaced the submission's single-run point estimates, plus a second same-config training run of every one of those seven rows. Two commands reproduce the manuscript: \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}derive\_\allowbreak{}metrics.py} turns the raw reports into \texttt{derived\_metrics.json}, and \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}verify\_\allowbreak{}paper\_\allowbreak{}numbers.py} asserts every quoted value against it. The audit script is written to \emph{fail}: it currently checks $1{,}245$ claims, treats a claim whose supporting artifact is missing as a failure rather than skipping it, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. \textbf{It also asserts what the records \emph{contain} and not only how many there are}, which is a change this revision made after the count-only version reported $869/869$ while the sentence above it made a false claim about the schema. That check immediately found a second instance of the same defect: the $438$-record gap between the scored deltas and the full action pairs is the three cross-corpus runs of Section~\ref{sec:cross_corpus}, written by an earlier harness that stored $\Delta_\infty$ and $\Delta_{L_1}$ without the action pair or the edit metadata. Their $\mathcal{F}$ is recomputable from the release; the individual edits behind it are not, so those three runs are reproducible at the aggregate level only, and we say so rather than let a uniform record count imply otherwise. \texttt{DATASHEET.md} follows \citet{datasheets} and states the release's known gaps as first-class content --- the calibration nulls on all 11 models in both architecture families, with \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} inapplicable by construction on the three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints rather than missing, edit error bars from 3 sampling seeds \emph{and} a same-config retraining replicate on every one of the seven trained rows, no rollout records behind any published number (the four-suite gate is released as a harness validation, not as a metric), P3 re-run in-domain on one model with a negative result, per-family $N$ varying from $60$ to $100$ --- alongside an explicit list of uses the artifact does not support. \texttt{LICENSE} places our code under MIT and our measurement records under CC~BY~4.0, and enumerates the upstream licenses of the $6$ corpora and $9$ checkpoints this release depends on and does not relicense. Those licenses were resolved from the Hugging Face Hub API by \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}fetch\_\allowbreak{}upstream\_\allowbreak{}licenses.py} rather than written from memory, and the machine-readable record with each repo's pinned commit sha is released as \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}license\_\allowbreak{}report.json}; the audit script asserts \texttt{LICENSE} and \texttt{DATASHEET.md} against it, having already caught two errors in our own earlier table (Bridge~V2 and BC-Z listed as CC~BY~4.0 when the LeRobot re-hosts we actually load are Apache-2.0, and two named source repos that no configuration in the release resolves). $3$ of the $15$ assets --- all three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints --- declare no license upstream at all; we disclose that verbatim and grant no rights to them rather than assign a license we cannot verify. Superseded runs are retained under \texttt{results\_v2/superseded/} with a README naming what replaced each, so the release keeps an audit trail rather than silently overwriting history. An anonymized public mirror will be linked at camera-ready.
